Hi there, I hope this message finds you well, I know these forms probably get a lot of traffic so I'll try to give as much context as possible even though I'm aware this is going to be a long email. So we are a mid-sized logistics company based in the Midwest, we've been around for about fourteen years now, started as a small trucking outfit and grew into a full third-party logistics provider with warehouses in three states. Over the last couple of years we've noticed our internal reporting systems have become a real mess, we have data coming in from our TMS, our WMS, an old Access database that one of our long time employees built back in like 2009, and a handful of spreadsheets that get emailed around every week. Every department seems to have their own version of the truth and it's causing a lot of friction between operations and finance especially around billing reconciliation. We tried to fix this internally last year with a hire but that person left after five months and we're back to square one. My business partner mentioned that a consultancy like yours might be able to come in and do an assessment first before we commit to any kind of platform decision, because honestly we don't even know if we need a new system or just better integration between what we have. We're not in a massive rush, our fiscal year ends in June so ideally we'd want any project to kick off sometime in Q2, but I wanted to reach out now to start the conversation and see what your discovery process typically looks like, what it costs, and how long it usually takes for a company our size. Would love to hop on a call whenever convenient. Thanks so much, Denise Whitfield, Ops Director at Cargill Route Logistics.

To whom it may concern, I am writing on behalf of my father who owns a small chain of hardware stores and recently engaged your firm for a supply chain optimization project, I believe the engagement was set up by my brother-in-law who handles most of the vendor relationships for the business, though I wasn't directly involved in the initial contract discussions so I apologize in advance if some of what I'm about to describe is already known to your team. Over the past three weeks since the project kicked off we have had nothing but issues, the consultant assigned to us, I think his name started with a T, has missed two scheduled check in calls without any notice, and when we finally did connect he seemed unfamiliar with the specifics of our inventory system which was strange because we had sent over documentation weeks in advance. On top of that the invoice we received last week included charges for hours that don't line up with anything we discussed, there's a line item for something called 'stakeholder alignment workshop' that never happened as far as anyone here can tell. My father is quite upset about this because this is a significant investment for a business our size and he was under the impression that this consultancy had a strong reputation, which is why he was referred by a friend in the building materials industry. We would like someone to review the account, correct the invoice, and ideally assign a different consultant going forward if that Tsomething person remains unavailable or unresponsive. Please treat this with some urgency as my father is considering canceling the engagement entirely if this isn't resolved soon. Thank you, Marcus Reilly.

I want to be upfront that our budget for this particular line item is quite limited compared to what I imagine a typical corporate client might spend with your firm, we're looking at something in the range of eight to twelve thousand dollars total, and I don't know if that's even in the realm of what would make sense for you to take on given that I've seen mentions online of your firm working with fairly large companies. That said, I figured it couldn't hurt to ask, and if it's not a good fit I would really appreciate it if you could point me toward the kind of consultancy that might be more appropriate for an organization of our size, since navigating this space has honestly been overwhelming for someone like me who came from a teaching background and not a business one. We do have some flexibility on timeline, the grant money needs to be allocated by the end of the calendar year but the actual work could happen into next spring. Any guidance you can offer, even if it's just a referral, would mean a lot to us. Warm regards, Priya Chandrasekaran, Program Director, Literacy Bridge Alliance.
